points.why: It says parameter 2 alone explains about 60% of the variance and dominates.
It gives parameter 1's 10% alone against its 0.40 total, attributes 30 points to interaction, and checks this against S2 = 0.28.
It warns that a one-at-a-time swing would make parameter 1 look irrelevant, says to pin down parameter 2 first, and says not to drop parameter 1.
It treats the indices as sample estimates, cites sampling error of about ±0.1, and recommends an adequate sample size.

notes: Minor notation slips (writing 'S1 + S1 + S2' and labeling parameter 2's index 'S1 = 0.60') and a meaningless remark about third-order effects in a two-parameter model, none of which change the interpretation.
